basic_information.name: Gemini Embedding (gemini-embedding-001)
basic_information.creator: Google DeepMind / Google Cloud
basic_information.description: Google's state-of-the-art text embedding model built on top of the Gemini large language model, achieving #1 rank on the MTEB Multilingual leaderboard with a mean task score of 68.32 across 100+ languages. Gemini Embedding is initialized from Gemini and fine-tuned with contrastive learning on a curated dataset that uses Gemini itself for data filtering, positive/negative passage selection, and synthetic data generation. The model uses Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) to produce flexible-dimension embeddings (128 to 3072 dimensions) and supports multiple task types including retrieval, classification, clustering, and semantic similarity. Available through both the Gemini API (Google AI Studio) and Vertex AI, it replaces the previous text-embedding-004 model. Key differentiators include top-tier multilingual performance, competitive pricing at $0.15/1M tokens, a generous free tier, and seamless integration with the Google Cloud ecosystem. The accompanying technical paper (arXiv:2503.07891) details training methodology and benchmark results.
basic_information.license: Proprietary (API-only access). No open model weights. Available through Google AI Gemini API and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Google's Terms of Service and Data Processing Addendum apply. EmbeddingGemma (separate open-source model, 300M parameters) is available on Hugging Face under open license but is a different, smaller model.
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary API model. Google's generative-ai-docs repository (examples and tutorials) and googleapis/python-genai SDK are open-source. EmbeddingGemma on Hugging Face is a separate open-source variant. No standalone repository for the Gemini Embedding model.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud API (serverless) via Gemini API (Google AI Studio) and Vertex AI. The model is initialized from Gemini LLM and uses mean pooling over token embeddings followed by a randomly initialized linear projection to the target embedding dimension. Supports task-specific prompts (inherited from the Gecko embedding line) and a pre-finetuning stage to enhance performance. Serverless auto-scaling on Google infrastructure. Also accessible through Vertex AI on Google Cloud with enterprise controls.
technical_architecture.language: Model implementation undisclosed (likely built on Google's internal JAX/TPU infrastructure). Client SDKs available in Python (google-genai, google-generativeai), JavaScript/TypeScript (@google/generative-ai), Go, Dart/Flutter, Swift, and Android. REST API available. Also accessible via Vertex AI SDK, BigQuery ML, and Firebase AI Logic.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Default: 3072 dimensions. Supports Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) for flexible dimension reduction. Recommended dimensions: 768, 1536, or 3072. Configurable via 'output_dimensionality' API parameter from 128 to 3072. Performance at 768d: MTEB 67.99; at 1536d: MTEB 68.17; at 3072d: MTEB 68.32 — demonstrating minimal degradation at lower dimensions.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — Gemini Embedding is a pure embedding generation model, not a vector database. Produces dense vector embeddings compatible with any indexing algorithm (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, flat, PQ, binary quantization) in any vector store. Google offers Vertex AI Vector Search (formerly Matching Engine) as a companion managed indexing service using ScaNN. Also natively integrated with AlloyDB (PostgreSQL-compatible) for vector search in BigQuery.
technical_architecture.scalability: Serverless API with automatic scaling. Free tier: 100 RPM (requests per minute), 1,000 RPD (requests per day). Paid tier rate limits vary by project configuration. Each request can include up to 250 input texts with a 20,000 token per request limit. Per-text limit: 2,048 input tokens (only first 2,048 tokens used per text). Batch API available for higher throughput at 50% of standard embedding price. Vertex AI quotas are configurable per project.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Gemini API (Google AI Studio) for developers and prototyping. Vertex AI (Google Cloud) for enterprise with VPC Service Controls, IAM, and compliance. BigQuery ML (in-place embedding of data warehouse content). Firebase AI Logic (mobile and web apps). Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) for on-premises deployment — Gemini models available on GDC with public preview starting Q3 2025 in partnership with NVIDIA Blackwell. Serverless Cloud Run integration for custom applications. No self-hosted model weights (proprietary).

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval. Produces dense embeddings optimized for cosine similarity and dot product similarity. Supports task-type-specific encoding via the 'task_type' parameter: RETRIEVAL_QUERY, RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT, SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY, CLASSIFICATION, CLUSTERING, CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY, QUESTION_ANSWERING, FACT_VERIFICATION. Query-document asymmetric embeddings improve retrieval quality when correct task types are specified. No native sparse vector (BM25/SPLADE) generation, but can be combined with BM25 for hybrid search through orchestration frameworks.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: N/A — embedding model is agnostic to chunking strategy. Works with any chunking approach. The 2,048-token input limit means documents exceeding this length require chunking. Compatible with all chunking frameworks (LangChain text splitters, LlamaIndex node parsers, Unstructured). Google's Vertex AI RAG Engine handles document parsing and chunking automatically. For comparison, Cohere Embed v4 supports 128K tokens and Voyage supports 32K tokens, making Gemini Embedding's context window relatively limited.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: No built-in reranking model. Google does not offer a dedicated reranking API comparable to Cohere Rerank. However, Gemini Embedding can be used in a two-stage retrieval pipeline with third-party rerankers (Cohere Rerank, cross-encoders, ColBERT). The Vertex AI RAG Engine supports reranking workflows. Google's documentation mentions HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) query transformation and multi-query retrieval as advanced retrieval techniques compatible with the model.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Gemini Embedding (gemini-embedding-001) is text-only. However, Google provides a separate Multimodal Embeddings model on Vertex AI (multimodalembedding@001) that generates 1408-dimension vectors for images, text, and video in the same semantic space. These are distinct models. Text and image embeddings from the multimodal model enable cross-modal retrieval (text-to-image, image-to-text). For multimodal RAG, the multimodal embeddings model is used alongside Gemini Embedding. No audio embedding support.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native graph capabilities. Gemini Embedding produces vector embeddings only. Knowledge graph construction, entity extraction, and graph-enhanced retrieval must be implemented externally. Google Cloud offers a managed Knowledge Graph API and BigQuery supports graph queries, but these are separate services not integrated with the embedding model. Compatible with graph RAG frameworks like Microsoft's GraphRAG or LlamaIndex's KnowledgeGraphIndex through the embedding pipeline.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in citation/grounding in the embedding model itself. However, when used with Gemini LLMs (Gemini 1.5/2.0/3.0) for RAG generation, Google provides grounding capabilities through Search Grounding (connecting to Google Search) and Vertex AI Grounding. The Vertex AI RAG Engine includes source attribution in generated responses. Citation generation is an application-layer responsibility when using embeddings alone.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Input token limit: 2,048 tokens per text (only first 2,048 tokens used). This is shorter than competitors (OpenAI text-embedding-3: 8,191 tokens; Cohere Embed v4: 128K tokens; Voyage-3: 32K tokens). For long documents, external chunking and summarization strategies are required. Matryoshka dimension reduction (3072 to 768 or lower) enables storage optimization without re-embedding. Google recommends using the Vertex AI RAG Engine for automatic context optimization including chunking, retrieval, and context selection.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Sub-second latency for typical workloads. Reported median latency: ~420ms for conversational embedding use cases (Mindlid). Average API latency: ~304ms with median of 273ms based on monitoring data. Latency depends on input length, batch size, and whether using Gemini API or Vertex AI. Batch API trades latency for throughput and cost savings (50% price reduction). [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Up to 250 texts per request with 20,000 tokens per request limit. Free tier: 100 RPM / 1,000 RPD. Paid tier rate limits configurable per project via Vertex AI quotas. Batch API available for high-throughput workloads. One benchmark reported embedding 100 emails in 21.45 seconds (90.4% faster than Voyage-2). Specific QPS numbers for production workloads not publicly disclosed by Google. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) Multilingual overall mean score: 68.32 at 3072 dimensions, 68.17 at 1536 dimensions, 67.99 at 768 dimensions. Task-specific MTEB scores: Pair Classification 85.13, Retrieval 67.71, Reranking 65.58, Classification +9.6 above second-best, Clustering +3.7 above second-best, Retrieval +9.0 above second-best. Achieved highest Borda rank across all task types on MMTEB (Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark covering 250+ languages). In independent testing: 87% accuracy in legal document retrieval (Everlaw, 1.4M documents), 82% top-3 recall (Mindlid wellness assistant, 4% lift over OpenAI text-embedding-3-small), 71.5% accuracy in general benchmark comparison (AiMultiple, 2026).
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: MTEB Multilingual leaderboard: #1 position since March 2025. Mean task score 68.32 (3072d). Substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art across MMTEB's 100+ tasks spanning 250+ languages. Compared to competitors on MTEB: Cohere Embed v4 65.2%, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large 64.6%, BGE-M3 63.0%. Note that NV-Embed (NVIDIA, October 2025) scored 69.32 on English-only MTEB and Qwen3-Embedding-8B scored 70.58 on MTEB Multilingual (January 2026), so the #1 position may be contested on some subsets. The arxiv paper (2503.07891) provides detailed per-task breakdowns across classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS, and summarization tasks.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Strong framework integration: LangChain (GoogleGenerativeAIEmbeddings class in langchain-google-genai package, also VertexAIEmbeddings in langchain-google-vertexai), LlamaIndex (GeminiEmbedding in llama-index-embeddings-gemini, with Vertex AI RAG tutorials), Haystack (GoogleAIGeminiGenerator integration), DSPy (Google AI integration). Also natively integrated with vector databases: Weaviate, Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, Chroma, and pgvector all have Google embedding examples or connectors. BigQuery ML supports in-place embedding generation using Gemini models.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Produces standard dense vectors usable with any LLM for RAG generation. Most naturally paired with Google's own Gemini models (1.5 Pro, 2.0 Flash, 3.0) which include Search Grounding and citation capabilities. Equally compatible with OpenAI GPT-4o, Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Meta Llama, and any other LLM. Works with any vector database that supports dense vectors. The Vertex AI RAG Engine provides an integrated pipeline with Gemini models.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Google supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) through the Gemini CLI and Agent Development Kit (ADK). Third-party MCP server implementations exist for Gemini API (aliargun/mcp-server-gemini, bsmi021/mcp-gemini-server on GitHub) that expose embedding capabilities as MCP tools. The Gemini CLI natively supports connecting to MCP servers. MCP integration is actively evolving in 2025-2026 within the broader Google AI ecosystem.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Gemini Embedding API is a pure embedding generation API — data source connectivity is handled by orchestration frameworks. Through Vertex AI RAG Engine, automatic integration with Google Cloud Storage (GCS), BigQuery, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner, Datastore, and Jira. Through LangChain/LlamaIndex, compatible with all standard data source loaders: S3, GCS, Confluence, Notion, Slack, databases, web crawl, APIs. BigQuery ML enables embedding generation directly on data warehouse content without data export.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Google Cloud provides built-in monitoring through Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, and Cloud Trace for Vertex AI API calls. Vertex AI Model Monitoring supports drift detection. Compatible with third-party observability platforms through LangChain/LlamaIndex instrumentation: LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix all support Google embedding call tracing. OpenTelemetry integration available through Google Cloud's operations suite.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Pay-per-token for API usage. $0.15 per 1 million input tokens (paid tier). Batch API: $0.075 per 1 million input tokens (50% discount, higher latency). Free tier available for development and small-scale use. No subscription, per-seat, or per-vector fees for API access. Vertex AI pricing may differ slightly with enterprise commitments.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Gemini API free tier: 100 RPM (requests per minute), 1,000 RPD (requests per day) — generous for prototyping and small-scale RAG experiments. The previous text-embedding-004 model was completely free for both input and output (being deprecated August 2025). The free tier is accessible via Google AI Studio without a Google Cloud billing account.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: At $0.15/1M tokens: 1M documents (~500 tokens each = 500M tokens) costs $75. 10M documents: $750. 100M documents: $7,500. With Batch API at $0.075/1M tokens: costs halved ($37.50 / $375 / $3,750). Cost comparison: more expensive than Voyage-3 ($0.06/1M tokens) and OpenAI text-embedding-3-small ($0.02/1M), but comparable to OpenAI text-embedding-3-large ($0.13/1M) and cheaper than Cohere Embed v4 images ($0.47/1M). Using 768 dimensions instead of 3072 reduces vector storage costs by 4x with minimal quality loss (MTEB drops from 68.32 to 67.99).
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Full RAG pipeline TCO with Google stack: Gemini Embedding ($0.15/1M tokens for embedding) + Vertex AI Vector Search or AlloyDB ($0.20-1.00+/hour depending on machine type) + Gemini LLM for generation ($0.15-1.25/1M input tokens depending on model). Vector storage: at 768 dimensions, 1M vectors require ~3GB, costing $5-20/month on managed services. Using Matryoshka dimension reduction and the Batch API can significantly reduce costs. Google Cloud's sustained use discounts and committed use contracts can reduce Vertex AI costs by 20-57%. The free tier makes prototyping effectively free.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader on MTEB Multilingual leaderboard since March 2025 (though position contested by Qwen3-Embedding and NV-Embed on some subsets as of early 2026). Strong position in the enterprise embedding market due to integration with the broader Google Cloud ecosystem (Vertex AI, BigQuery, AlloyDB, GKE). Primary competitor to OpenAI's embedding models for cloud API users. Google's massive infrastructure and global reach give it natural advantages for multilingual and large-scale deployments. Positioned as the premium multilingual embedding option.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Everlaw (legal discovery): 87% accuracy on 1.4M documents with complex legal terms. Re:cap (financial analytics): significant F1 score improvements over previous Google models. Roo Code (open-source AI coding assistant): powers codebase indexing and semantic search. Mindlid (AI wellness companion): sub-second latency with 82% top-3 recall. Interaction Co. (Poke email assistant): 90.4% faster embedding time vs competitors. Broader Google Cloud Vertex AI customer base includes many Fortune 500 companies using Google's AI infrastructure.
adoption_and_market.community_size: Google's AI developer community is massive. Google AI Studio serves millions of developers. Vertex AI has enterprise-scale adoption. The google-generativeai Python package has significant monthly downloads. Google Developer Forums and Stack Overflow have active Gemini embedding discussions. The arxiv paper (2503.07891) has generated significant academic and industry attention. No dedicated Discord/Slack community specifically for the embedding model, but general Google AI communities are large.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Gemini Embedding is a product of Google DeepMind / Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG). Alphabet's market capitalization exceeds $2 trillion. Google Cloud revenue reached $43.8 billion in FY2024 with AI being a major growth driver. Google invests tens of billions annually in AI R&D. Not a startup funding scenario — this is a product from one of the world's largest technology companies.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (market leader by adoption, 64.6% MTEB, 8K token context, $0.13/1M tokens), Cohere Embed v4 (65.2% MTEB, 128K context, multimodal, enterprise deployment flexibility), Voyage-3/4 (acquired by Google/Alphabet, strong domain-specific models, $0.06-0.18/1M tokens), Amazon Titan Embeddings (AWS ecosystem), Mistral Embed (77.8% accuracy in some benchmarks). Open-source alternatives: Qwen3-Embedding-8B (70.58% MTEB Multilingual), NV-Embed (69.32% MTEB English), BGE-M3 (BAAI, 63.0%), E5 (Microsoft), GTE (Alibaba), Nomic Embed — several match or exceed Gemini on specific benchmarks at zero API cost. Google differentiates via: top multilingual coverage (100+ languages), Matryoshka flexible dimensions, deep GCP ecosystem integration, generous free tier, Batch API at 50% cost, and the backing of world-class AI research (DeepMind).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best for: startups building multilingual products (100+ languages natively), teams already on Google Cloud Platform, and applications requiring strong general-purpose embeddings without domain-specific fine-tuning. The generous free tier (100 RPM / 1,000 RPD) makes it excellent for bootstrapped startups prototyping RAG systems at zero cost. Team size: works for solo developers through large teams — the managed API removes infrastructure complexity. Budget: the $0.15/1M token pricing is mid-range, making it affordable for most startups. Consider for: multilingual SaaS products, Google Workspace integrations, Firebase-based mobile apps with RAG features. Less ideal for: teams requiring on-premise deployment (limited GDC availability), very long documents without chunking (2K token limit vs 128K for Cohere v4), or teams needing integrated reranking (no Google reranking model).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Gemini Embedding API (buy) when: you need top-tier multilingual embeddings, your stack is on GCP/Google Cloud, you want the simplest possible integration (single API call), or you need a generous free tier for prototyping. Use Vertex AI RAG Engine (managed buy) when: you want a fully managed RAG pipeline without managing vector databases. Consider open-source alternatives when: API costs are prohibitive at scale (Qwen3-Embedding, BGE-M3, NV-Embed are free and competitive), you need fine-tuning for a specific domain, or you need on-premise deployment. Migration note: switching embedding models requires re-embedding your entire corpus, as embeddings from different providers are not interchangeable — choose carefully before production deployment.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 15-30 minutes (pip install google-generativeai + simple API call with task_type parameter). MVP with full RAG pipeline using LangChain/LlamaIndex: 1-3 days. Production deployment on Vertex AI: 1-3 weeks including error handling, rate limit management, monitoring, and VPC Service Controls. BigQuery ML in-place embedding: 1-2 days for teams already using BigQuery. Firebase AI Logic integration for mobile apps: 2-5 days.
key_lessons: 1. Use the task_type parameter correctly — specifying RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT for indexing and RETRIEVAL_QUERY for queries significantly improves retrieval quality vs using a generic task type. This is free performance that many developers miss.

2. Start with 768 dimensions instead of 3072 — Matryoshka training means 768-dim vectors achieve 67.99 MTEB vs 68.32 at 3072d (only 0.5% difference) while using 4x less storage. This is a 4x reduction in vector database costs with minimal quality impact. Only increase dimensions if measured retrieval quality demands it.

3. Leverage the free tier and Batch API aggressively — the free tier (100 RPM / 1,000 RPD) is sufficient for early-stage development, and the Batch API at 50% cost ($0.075/1M tokens) should be used for all corpus embedding. Real-time embedding at full price should be reserved for query-time only.

4. Plan for the 2,048-token input limit — this is significantly shorter than competitors (OpenAI 8K, Cohere 128K). Design your chunking strategy accordingly, targeting 500-1500 token chunks. For long documents, consider using the multimodal embedding model or combining with document summarization.

5. Consider the Google ecosystem lock-in tradeoff — Gemini Embedding integrates beautifully with GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery, AlloyDB, Firebase) but creates dependency on Google's infrastructure. If multi-cloud flexibility or data sovereignty outside Google is important, consider Cohere (multi-cloud) or open-source models (full control). Embedding migration is expensive — it requires re-embedding your entire corpus.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Google AI Studio provides a web-based playground for testing embeddings. Vertex AI Studio offers a visual interface for experimenting with embedding models. BigQuery ML enables embedding generation via SQL queries without code. Firebase AI Logic provides SDKs for mobile integration. Third-party no-code platforms (Flowise, Dify, AnythingLLM, n8n, Make) integrate with the Gemini API for visual RAG pipeline construction. The Vertex AI RAG Engine provides a managed pipeline that reduces code requirements significantly.

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from Google Developers Blog official announcements, Google Cloud documentation (Vertex AI, Gemini API), the arxiv technical paper (2503.07891), Google AI for Developers documentation, independent benchmark comparisons (VentureBeat, WinBuzzer, AiMultiple, Modal), pricing pages (Google AI, Vertex AI), customer case studies (Everlaw, Re:cap, Roo Code, Mindlid, Interaction Co.), and the MTEB leaderboard on Hugging Face.
confidence.cross_reference: MTEB score of 68.32 confirmed across Google Developers Blog, VentureBeat, WinBuzzer, OpenTools.ai, arxiv paper, and OpenRouter. Pricing of $0.15/1M tokens confirmed across Google AI pricing page, CometAPI, MarkTechPost, and multiple third-party calculators. 2,048-token input limit confirmed across Vertex AI documentation, MarkTechPost, and Google Developer Forums. MRL support and 3072-dimension output confirmed across Google docs, arxiv paper, and Skywork.ai. Customer testimonials confirmed from Google Developers Blog (GA announcement). Free tier limits confirmed across Google AI docs and Spurnow analysis.
confidence.caveats: The #1 MTEB position may be contested — Qwen3-Embedding-8B (January 2026, 70.58 MTEB Multilingual) and NV-Embed (October 2025, 69.32 MTEB English) both score higher on certain subsets. MTEB leaderboard rankings are volatile with frequent new submissions. The 2,048-token input limit is significantly shorter than competitors (OpenAI 8K, Voyage 32K, Cohere 128K), which may be a dealbreaker for long-document use cases. Google Distributed Cloud (on-premise) deployment for Gemini models was in preview as of Q3 2025 — production availability for embedding specifically is uncertain. Latency and throughput numbers are from third-party reports, not official Google benchmarks. The experimental model (gemini-embedding-exp-03-07) had an 8K token limit but the GA model reverted to 2K — future versions may increase this.
confidence.security_posture: Google Cloud platform is SOC 1/2/3 Type II certified, ISO 27001/27017/27018 compliant, FedRAMP High authorized, HIPAA compliant (with BAA), and GDPR compliant. Vertex AI offers VPC Service Controls for network isolation, IAM for access control, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK), and audit logging. Zero Data Retention available on Vertex AI — customer data is not used for model training. Data encrypted at rest and in transit. ISO 42001 certification for AI management achieved May 2025. Known general embedding risks: embedding vectors can theoretically be inverted to approximate original text (embedding inversion attacks), which is a general risk across all embedding models. Google's enterprise security posture is among the strongest in the industry.
